doc: Ascent of a northern tropical storm (radius 0.06, weight 1.6): a dense ring gaussian of radius 0.6 r = 0.036 minus a clear eye 1.6 exp(-d2 / (0.12 r)^2), on a 41 x 41 float32 patch whose central texel is exactly the center, where the eye depth shows (1 - 1.6). Tolerance rtol 2e-4, atol 2e-5: the eye gaussian has a radius of 0.0072, so the float32 subtraction p - c next to the center moves the exponent: the float64-promoted computation differs by at most 6e-6 and a one-ulp nudge of the directions by 1.8e-5 (1.96 of the default band); tolerance 10 times that. Conventions of cloudgen.sphere read here: lonlat_to_dir(lon, lat) = (cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat) with float64 numpy cos and sin (right-handed, z north, longitude grows east; a vortex center is that direction); normalize(v) = v / |v| (plain division, no epsilon: a zero vector gives NaN).

params.dtype_chain: p float32: a = float32 zeros; per vortex the center is cast to float32, d2, exp and the gaussians are float32 (a cyclone takes _comma_ascent, float32; a tropical subtracts its float32 eye); the term is np.float32(ascent) * g.astype(float32) and a += term accumulates in float32, in vortex order.
